name: Reuters
description: International news agency covering general news and business.
significance: Useful for international and financial news coverage.
signals: Publishes journalistic standards covering accuracy, independence and corrections. Publisher-stated policies, not an independent reliability audit.

name: Associated Press
description: Global news organization supplying reporting across many subjects.
significance: Useful for general news and distributed news coverage.
signals: Publishes news values and reporting practices addressing accuracy and bias. These policies do not guarantee an individual article.

name: Ars Technica
description: Specialist technology publication founded in 1998, with news, reviews and analysis.
significance: Particularly useful for technology and IT audiences; specialist relevance can matter more than general prominence.
signals: Documents its editorial mission and specialist focus. This establishes outlet context, not independent proof of accuracy.

name: ABC News (US)
description: US-based news organization with international reporting operations.
significance: Broad public-news coverage, rather than a single industry focus.
signals: Disney documents editorial-independence, accuracy, correction and ethics-training commitments for ABC News. These are publisher-stated safeguards.

name: ESPN
significance: Useful for sports reporting and sports-industry coverage.
signals: Disney documents editorial guidelines and ESPN Editorial Board oversight. Individual stories and commercial relationships still need evaluation.

name: WIRED
description: Publication covering the effects of technology and science on business, politics and culture.
significance: Useful for technology's wider social and industry impact.
signals: Describes reporting assignments and identifies subject editors. This is an editorial-transparency signal, not a reliability certification.

name: The Verge
significance: Useful for technology news and product coverage.
signals: Publishes an ethics statement addressing editorial independence and conflicts. Evaluate the article's evidence as well as the outlet's policy.

name: The Guardian
signals: Documents its newsroom mission and trust ownership.

name: NBC News
signals: Identifies its news programs and organization.
